items.title: How Chinese AI Firms Tried to Clone U.S. AI Models
items.summary: Anthropic says DeepSeek and Moonshot used thousands of fake accounts and millions of real user queries to run "distillation" campaigns aimed at cloning its AI capabilities. Anthropic also said Moonshot secretly routed some user requests to Claude while presenting the responses as its own model's output.
items.why_it_matters: It escalates the US-China fight over AI intellectual property and raises questions about how labs can protect frontier models from being cloned via their own APIs.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra: The next generation in intelligence for work
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Astra, described as its most capable model yet for business use, with advanced reasoning, computer-use capabilities, and stronger writing and design judgment.
items.why_it_matters: A new flagship frontier model from OpenAI resets the bar for enterprise AI capability and competitive pressure on rival labs.

items.title: The AI Researcher Who Just Quit Anthropic Says It's 'Crunch Time for Humanity'
items.summary: Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned and told Wired about a "mini Manhattan project" inside the company, arguing AI labs have only a few years left to make their systems safe. He discussed the unresolved alignment problem and the pressure of racing rivals, and the story landed amid a wider wave of Anthropic and OpenAI staff voicing similar fears.
items.why_it_matters: A safety researcher publicly breaking from a leading AI lab intensifies pressure for coordinated regulation of frontier AI development.

items.title: Mathematicians want proof OpenAI didn't use their work
items.summary: A second mathematician has come forward accusing OpenAI of unethical and "dishonest" behavior and a lack of transparency about the data behind its claimed Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize solution. This follows an earlier row over whether the model benefited from unpublished mathematical work.
items.why_it_matters: The credibility fight over how OpenAI's models got their training data could determine whether the landmark math claim is trusted by the field.

items.title: Anthropic Says It Blocked Possible Efforts to Build Biological Weapons
items.summary: Anthropic disclosed in a new report that it blocked possible attempts to use its AI models to help build biological weapons. The company said it could not determine whether the underlying research was legitimate or nefarious, and shut the work down as a precaution.
items.why_it_matters: It shows a frontier lab is actively finding and cutting off attempts to misuse its models for the most catastrophic risks, adding urgency to the safety debate.

items.title: Google Picks Chilly Finland for €13 Billion European AI Buildout
items.summary: Google is spending €13 billion ($15.1 billion) on AI infrastructure in Finland, its biggest-ever European investment. Bloomberg notes the country's cold climate and carbon-free power make it attractive for data center builders.
items.why_it_matters: It is one of the largest single AI infrastructure commitments in Europe and signals where hyperscalers see the best economics for AI capacity.

items.title: Introducing the Agents API
items.summary: OpenAI launched the Agents API, a managed service powered by the Codex harness for building and running cloud agents, supporting orchestration, long-running sessions, and tool use.
items.why_it_matters: It gives developers an official, managed way to build persistent AI agents, a core building block for the next wave of AI products.

items.title: Google DeepMind Uses AI to Predict 9 Billion DNA Changes
items.summary: Google DeepMind built an AI system that predicts the effects of roughly 9 billion possible single-base changes across the human genome. The lab says it hopes the model will help researchers uncover the genetic causes of disease.
items.why_it_matters: Comprehensive genome-wide prediction at this scale could speed up discovery of disease-causing mutations for medical research.

items.title: Microsoft AI Focused Data Center Plan to Add 26 Gigawatts of Compute
items.summary: Microsoft is planning to add 26 gigawatts of AI-focused data center compute, building toward 38 gigawatts of total capacity. The company said shortages had forced it to turn away some AI and cloud business.
items.why_it_matters: The scale of the buildout shows how far current data center capacity still lags the demand for AI compute among hyperscalers.

items.title: OpenAI not on track to reduce risk of 'catastrophic' loss of control, says board member
items.summary: Paul Christiano, a US government technology adviser who has joined OpenAI's non-profit foundation board, said there is "a meaningful risk that rapid acceleration in AI capabilities leads to catastrophic and irreversible loss of control in the very near term," and that OpenAI is not on track to reduce that risk to an acceptable level.
items.why_it_matters: A newly appointed OpenAI board member publicly questioning the company's own safety trajectory adds weight to the industry-wide debate over AI risk.
